method: 4-summand relation collection (examples/prime_fast_j0_sym.rs summands=4), extension of frozen_sym4_holdout.json to 36 and 38 bits
holdout_command: CSKIP=1300 NOPLAIN2=1 C3=<baseline_c> prime_fast_j0_sym out.jsonl <bits> <B> 8 40 <4 or 3>
holdout: CSKIP=1300 (curves never used in tuning, debugging or the exploratory 36-bit run), 8 instances per arm per size, wall clock, one host, no isolation; each row times tuned ic_solve in-row (plain3_ms). The 3-summand arm uses B3 from the p^(1/3) scaling of the earlier tuned B3 and is not tuned at these sizes.
prediction: pooled sum(plain3_ms)/sum(sym4_ms) >= 18 (36 bits) and >= 25 (38 bits); all solves verified
abandon_rule: any pooled plain3/sym4 < 8 or any failed verification => the claim that the 4-summand advantage over tuned ic_solve grows to 36-38 bits is withdrawn
known_limits: 6-8 rows, one group per size, no isolation or A/A, baseline c at 36 bits on the grid edge, sym3 arm untuned, rho reference has a fixed overhead of about 2 ms
